title: Annotatio IV §.IV open: Antecedent Institution commentary succeeded by Pauline 1 Cor. 10–11
pass_a_gloss: §. IV. So stands the Antecedent Commentary on the Institution words of the Sacred Supper, giving both origin and foundation to the true sentence concerning it, composed by Christ Himself, which the Apostolic Successor receives — specially the Pauline chapters 1 Cor. 10 and 11. The former of these chapters supplies as many arguments as you please for the spiritual presence and participation of Christ’s body and blood, but none for the corporal.
pass_b_english: §.IV: Christ’s antecedent Institution commentary (origin and foundation of the true sentence) is succeeded by the Apostolic / Pauline commentary — specially 1 Cor. 10 and 11.
Chapter 10 supplies many arguments for spiritual presence and participation of body and blood — none for the corporal.
source_text: §. IV. Ita habet Commentarius verborum Institutionis S. Cœnæ Antecedaneus, Sententiæ de ea veræ tam originem dans, quàm fundamentum struens, ab ipso Christo confectus, quem excipit Succedaneus Apostolicus, speciatim Paulinus 1. Cor. 10. & 11. capp. Horum Capitum prius quàm plurima pro spirituali corporis & sanguinis Christi præsentia & participatione, nullum verò pro corporali suppeditat argumentum.
notes: §.IV open: Pauline successor to John 6 commentary.
